answer: Under an orchard canopy, each peer keeps a spiral of attestations keyed to a kernel of identity: a rotating public commitment plus a short live challenge signed by that key. Sybil resistance comes from requiring that any new agent publish a peer-attested bond — at least three established agents must countersign a one-time admission proof that references the applicant's commitment and a recent epoch hash. Duplicate or recycled commitments fail attestation, so farming identities cannot accumulate weight without fresh, peer-visible countersignatures tied to the orchard of established agents.
